Medinan, and it contains one thousand, seven hundred and ninety-two letters, four hundred and seventy-three words, and twenty-two verses.

Abu al-Husayn ʿAli ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri informed us, from Murrah, who said: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Jurjani and Abu al-Shaykh ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani narrated to us, and both said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Sharik al-Kufi narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Yarbuʿi narrated to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym al-Mada'ini narrated to us, who said: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mujadila, he will be written among the party of Allah on the Day of Resurrection." [228] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/407.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾

*Tukhasimuka* (she disputes with you), *tuhawiruka* (she converses with you), *turajiʿuka* (she returns to you with her plea) — "in her husband": she was a woman from the Ansar, then from the Khazraj. They differed about her name and lineage. Ibn ʿAbbas said: she was Khawlah bint Khuwaylid. Abu al-ʿAliyah said: Khuwaylah bint al-Dulaym. Qatadah said: Khuwaylah bint Thaʿlabah. The two Muqatils said:

Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah ibn Malik ibn Khizamah al-Khazrajiyyah, of the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.

ʿAtiyyah reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: Khawlah bint al-Samit.

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah reported, from his father, from ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that her name was Jamilah [[In the source: Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah.]], and her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit, brother of ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit. The reason was that she had a beautiful figure, and her husband saw her prostrating in her prayer and looked at her backside. When she finished, he wanted her, but she refused him, so he became angry with her. He was a man with quickness of temper and a touch of irritability.

He said to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother." Then he regretted what he had said. Zihar and iyla' were among the divorces of the people of the Jahiliyyah. He said to her: "I do not think you are anything but forbidden to me now." She said: "Do not say that; go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him." He said: "I find myself too shy to ask him about this." She said: "Then let me ask him." He said: "Ask him."

So she came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while ʿAʾishah was washing one side of his head. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband Aws ibn al-Samit married me when I was a young, beautiful woman with wealth and family. But when he consumed my wealth, wasted my youth, I was separated from my family and became old, he made zihar against me, and now he regrets it. Is there anything that could bring me and him together and revive me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have become forbidden to him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Him who sent down the Book to you, he did not mention divorce, and he is the father of my children and the dearest of people to me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of my poverty and my loneliness; my companionship has lasted long and I have borne him children [[As in the manuscript; in the source: "nathartu" (I have spread out)]]." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "I do not see you except as forbidden to him, and I have not been commanded anything regarding your case." [229] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/666, no. 2063; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 7/382; Mustadrak al-Hakim: 2/481.]]

She kept returning to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and each time he said to her, "You have become forbidden to him," she cried out and said: "I complain to Allah of my poverty and the severity of my condition. O Allah, send down [a revelation] upon the tongue of Your Prophet."

This was the first zihar in Islam. ʿAʾishah then came forward to wash the other side of his head and said: "Look into my matter, may Allah make me your ransom, O Prophet of Allah." ʿAʾishah said: "Shorten your speech and your conversation. Do you not see the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when revelation comes down to him, how he is seized like one in a deep sleep?" When the revelation ended, he said: "Call your husband." He came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to him what had been revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ Then he explained the ruling of zihar and made expiation (kaffarah) obligatory for it, saying, ﴿Those who make zihar among you from their wives﴾ to the end. ʿAʾishah said: "Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses all voices! The woman was speaking to the Messenger of Allah while I was in a corner of the house, hearing some of her words and some being hidden from me, when He, glorified be He, revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly heard…﴾ the verses."

When these verses were revealed and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited them to him, he said to him: "Can you free a slave?"

He said: "Then my wealth would all be gone. The slave is expensive, and I have little wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Can you fast two consecutive months?" He said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, if I do not eat three times a day, my eyesight goes dim, and I fear my eyes will become blind." He said: "Can you feed sixty needy persons?" He said: "No, by Allah, unless you help me with that, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will help you with fifteen sa'," and I pray for blessing for you." [231] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/409, with slight variation.]]

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helped him with fifteen sa', and their affair was settled.

This is His saying: ﴿Those who make zihar among you from their wives﴾. We have mentioned the differences of the readers regarding this word in Surat al-Ahzab.

*Ma hunna ummahatihim* — the majority of readers read it with a kasrah on the *ta'* (*ummahatihim*), and its position is in the accusative, like His saying: *ma hadha basharan* (Surah Yusuf 12:31). It was also said: (*bi-ummahatihim*). Al-Mufaddal read it with a dammah on the *ta'*. ﴿Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them, and indeed they utter an objectionable word and a falsehood.﴾ That is, a lie; *al-munkar* is that whose soundness is not known. ﴿And indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾

﴿Those who make zihar from their wives﴾: know that the expressions by which a man becomes one who makes zihar are of two kinds: explicit (sarih) and allusive (kinayah). The explicit form is that he says, "You are to me like the back of my mother." Likewise if he says, "You are to me like the belly of my mother, or like the head of my mother, or like the private part of my mother"; and similarly if he says, "Your private part, or your head, or your back, or your chest, or your belly, or your hand, or your leg is to me like the back of my mother," he becomes one who makes zihar. All of this falls under the same category as his saying, "Your hand, or your leg, or your head, or your belly is divorced," in which case she is divorced; the disagreement in this matter between the two groups is like the disagreement concerning divorce.

Whenever he likens her to his mother or to one of his grandmothers, paternal or maternal, it is zihar without disagreement. If he likens her to someone other than mother or grandmother from those unlawful women who are never lawful to him in any way, such as a daughter, sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, and the like, he is one who makes zihar according to the sound position of the schools. So the explicit zihar is that he likens his wife, or a part of her body, to a part of his mother's body, or to the body of one of his unlawful female relatives.

The allusive form is that he says, "You are to me like my mother," or "like my mother," or something similar; in this case his intention is taken into account. If he intends zihar, he is one who makes zihar; if he does not intend zihar, he does not become one who makes zihar. Every husband whose divorce is valid, his zihar is valid, whether he is a slave or free, a dhimmi, whether he has consummated the marriage or not, and whether he is able to have intercourse or unable. Likewise zihar is valid from every wife, whether young or old, sane or insane, one with a closed passage or a healthy one, fasting or in ihram, a dhimmiyyah or a Muslimah, or in a waiting period during which he may take her back.

Abu Hanifah said: the zihar of a dhimmi is not valid. Malik said: the zihar of a slave is not valid. Some scholars said: the zihar of one who has not consummated the marriage is not valid. Al-Muzani said: if a man divorces his wife with a revocable divorce and then makes zihar, it is not valid.

﴿Then they return to what they said.﴾ Know that expiation becomes obligatory by both zihar and return together, and it is not obligatory by one of them without the other, just as in the matter of oaths the expiation is obligatory by both the oath and the breaking of it together. So if he returns from his zihar, expiation becomes binding on him.

The scholars and jurists differed about the meaning of return (al-ʿawd). Al-Shafiʿi said: the return that makes expiation obligatory is that he withholds from divorcing her after the zihar, and a period passes in which he could have divorced her, but he does not divorce her.

Qatadah said: ﴿Then they return to what they said﴾ means he wishes to have intercourse with her and to sleep with her after he has made her unlawful. Abu Hanifah also took this view, saying: if he resolves to have intercourse with her and intends to approach her, it is a return.

Malik said: if he has intercourse with her, it is a return; if he does not have intercourse with her, it is not a return.

The Zahiris said: if he repeats the words, it is a return; if he does not repeat them, it is not a return. This is also the view of Abu al-ʿAliyah, and the apparent meaning of the verse supports it, namely His saying: ﴿Then they return to what they said﴾, that is, to what they said.

﴿Then the freeing of a [believing] neck [[As in the manuscript; the apparent meaning is that a word has dropped from the author's text, namely "mu'minah" (believing), explaining the slave, so that the reasoning holds.]] before they touch one another.﴾ Because Allah, glorified be He, restricted the neck to belief in the expiation for killing, and left it unrestricted in this place, and it is a rule that the unrestricted is to be understood in light of the restricted. His saying: ﴿before they touch one another﴾ means before they have intercourse. Intercourse itself is forbidden to the one who makes zihar until he makes expiation; if he has intercourse before expiating, he has committed a forbidden act, yet the expiation is not dropped from him, but he must perform it as a makeup (qada'), just as if he delayed prayer beyond its time, its performance is not dropped from him but its making up becomes obligatory. Whether he expiates by freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding, he must give precedence to the expiation, and it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with her before the expiation.

Abu Hanifah said: if he expiates by feeding, it is permissible for him to have intercourse and then feed; he did not differ regarding freeing or fasting.

This is the ruling on the intercourse of one who makes zihar before expiation.

As for other than intercourse, such as kissing and enjoyment (tal-adhdhudh), it is not forbidden according to the view of most scholars. This is the view of al-Hasan and Sufyan, and it is the sound position of al-Shafiʿi's school. Some said: it refers to all meanings of touching (al-masis), because it is general, and this is one of al-Shafiʿi's two opinions, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿That you are admonished with﴾: you are commanded with it. ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do.﴾ ﴿So whoever does not find [a slave]﴾, nor the price of one, or one who owns a slave but needs him for his service, or one who owns the price but needs it for his maintenance, or who has a dwelling in which he lives, then he may move on to fasting.

Abu Hanifah said: he is not permitted to fast, and he must free a slave even if he needs it and its price; if he is unable to find a slave, ﴿then fasting two consecutive months before they touch one another﴾. If he breaks the fast during it without an excuse, he breaks the consecutiveness and must begin two consecutive months anew. If he breaks it because of an excuse, such as illness or travel, the jurists differed about it. Some said: the consecutiveness is not broken, and he may continue and make up the remainder; this was the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah, ʿAmr ibn Dinar, and al-Shaʿbi, and it is one of al-Shafiʿi's two opinions.

Others said: he may not continue but must start over and begin afresh; this is the view of al-Nakhaʿi and his companions, and it is the more sound of al-Shafiʿi's two opinions.

If during the two months there intervenes a period in which fasting for expiation is not valid, such as the two festivals, the days of tashriq, and the days of Ramadan, the consecutiveness is broken by that, and a new start becomes obligatory.

If the one who makes zihar has intercourse during the two months, it is examined: if he has intercourse with her by day, the consecutiveness is broken and he must begin again; if he has intercourse with her by night, the consecutiveness is not broken. Abu Hanifah said: whether he has intercourse by night or by day, it breaks the consecutiveness, and he must begin two consecutive months anew.

﴿So whoever is not able to fast﴾: inability is such as fearing from fasting due to an ailment, or the onset of severe hardship and clear harm. ﴿Then feeding sixty needy persons﴾, for each needy person a mudd of the staple food of his region. The disagreement between the two groups about this is like the disagreement about the zakat al-fitr. ﴿That is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger; and these are the limits of Allah. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who oppose [yuhaddunna]: they oppose and act hostilely against Allah and His Messenger﴾. ﴿Kubitu﴾: they were destroyed, humiliated, and disgraced, ﴿as those before them were humiliated. And We have certainly sent down clear verses, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it, and Allah is Witness over all things.﴾ ﴿Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth? There is no private conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth, nor of fewer than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

The reading of the majority is *yakunu* with the *ya'* because of the intervening word; Abu Jaʿfar the reciter read *takunu* with the *ta'*, because *najwa* is feminine. The first is more eloquent and more correct. *Min najwa mutanajjin thalathah*: al-Farra' said: if you wish, you may put *thalathah* in the genitive as an adjective of *najwa*, and if you wish, you may make *najwa* annexed to it; and if you put it in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), it would be correct. *Illa huwa rabiʿuhum* — by knowledge: He hears their secret talk and knows its content. *Wa la khamsatin illa huwa sadisuhum wa la adna min dhalika wa la akthara* — the majority read it in the accusative, in the position of the genitive by coordination. Yaʿqub and Abu Hatim read *akthar* in the nominative, on the position of the statement before the entry of *min*. Al-Zuhri read *akbar* with the *ba'* (i.e., *akbar*). *Illa huwa maʿahum aynama kanu*. *Thumma yunabbi'uhum bima ʿamilu yawm al-qiyamah*. *Inna Allaha bikulli shay'in ʿalim.*

The scholars and jurists differed about the meaning of return (al-ʿawd). Al-Shafiʿi said: the return that makes expiation obligatory is that he withholds from divorcing her after the zihar, and a period passes in which he could have divorced her, but he does not divorce her.

﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel?﴾ (and the rest of the verse)

When the believers saw their secret consultations, they would say: "We see them only because news has reached them of our relatives and brothers who went out on the expeditions (sariyya) that they were killed, or died, or met some misfortune or defeat." This would fall upon their hearts and grieve them, and they would continue like this until their companions and relatives returned. When this went on for long and became frequent, they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he commanded them not to hold secret consultations apart from the Muslims. But they did not desist from this and returned to their secret consultations, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Muqatil said (the manuscript reads "Muqatilan," but the correct form is "al-Muqatilan"): It was revealed concerning the Jews. There was a truce (muwada'a) between them and the Prophet (ﷺ). Whenever a man from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) (peace be upon him) passed by them, they would sit and hold secret consultations among themselves, so that the believer would think they were conspiring to kill him or to do something he disliked. The believer would then take another road out of fear. This reached the Prophet (peace be upon him), and he forbade them from secret consultation, but they did not desist and returned to their secret consultation, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Zayd said: A man would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asking him for a need, so as to show the people that he had been in private conference with him. Then he would say to them: "They were only conferring about a war that has come, or a gathering that has been assembled against you, or an important matter that has occurred." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel?﴾, that is, private conversation (al-munajat).

Yahya, al-A'mash and Hamza read "yantajun" (ينتجون), on the pattern of "yaftaʿilun," while the rest read "yatanajawna" (يَتَناجَوْنَ), on the pattern of "yatafa'alun." Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the latter because of His saying: ﴿When you hold secret counsel﴾ and ﴿and they hold secret counsel,﴾ and He did not say "intajaytum" or "intajaw." Al-Dahhak read "wa-maʿsiyat al-rasul" (ومعصيات الرسول), with both words in the plural.

﴿When they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you, and they say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Hell will be enough for them; they will burn in it, and what an evil destination.﴾

He did not understand what they said, and "as-sam" means death. When they went out, they would say: "If he were a prophet, he would have been punished and our prayer against him would have been answered, and he would have known what we said." Then they came in to him one day and said: "As-sam ʿalayka." ʿAʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) understood their words and said: "And upon you be death, and disgrace, and affliction, and the curse." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be quiet, ʿAʾisha, for Allah, mighty and majestic, loves gentleness in all matters, and does not love obscenity and foul speech."

She said: "O Messenger of Allah, did you not hear what they said?" The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Did you not hear what I replied to them?" Then Allah revealed this verse. The common reading is "tatanajaw" with an alif. Ruways related from Yaʿqub: "fa-la tatanjaw" (فلا تتنجوا), from "al-intija'." ﴿in sin and enmity and disobedience to the Messenger﴾, like the deed of the hypocrites and Jews, ﴿but hold secret counsel in righteousness and piety. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us: Hammad ibn al-Hasan told us: ʿUbayd Allah told us: al-A'mash told us, from Sufyan, from ʿAbdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you are three, let not two of them confer apart from their companion (the manuscript reads 'sahibihi,' but 'sahibihima' is more correct), for that grieves him." [233] [Musnad Ahmad 1/375.]

Muhammad ibn Hamdun informed us: Makki informed us: Abdullah ibn Bishr informed us: Sufyan told us, from ʿAbdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let not two confer apart from a third." [234] [Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal 1/375, 425, 431, 432, 438, 462, 464.]

﴿O you who have believed, when it is said to you, "Make room" (tafassahu) in gatherings…﴾ the verse.

Qatadah said: They used to compete for places in the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ) (peace be upon him). When they saw someone coming toward them, they would begrudge him a place beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah commanded them to make room for one another.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to honor the People of Badr among the Emigrants and the Helpers. Some men from the People of Badr came, among them Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and they had arrived earlier at the gathering. They stood before the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah." The Prophet (peace be upon him) returned their greeting. Then they greeted the people after that, and they returned their greeting. Then they stood on their feet, waiting for room to be made for them. The Prophet (peace be upon him) understood what made them stand, but the people did not make room for them. This grieved the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said to those around him from the Emigrants, the Helpers and the Successors who were not of the People of Badr: "Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so." [235] [Zad al-Masir 7/323.]

So he made a number of people stand up equal to the group who had stood before him from the People of Badr. This grieved those who were made to rise from their places, and the Prophet (ﷺ) (peace be upon him) noticed the dislike on their faces. Then the hypocrites said to the Muslims: "Do you not claim that your companion is just among people? By Allah, he has not been just to these people. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn al-Shammas (this story has been mentioned in Surah al-Hujurat), and Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning the man who was not given room: ﴿O you who have believed, when it is said to you, "Make room" (tafassahu)﴾: spread out and widen. From this comes the saying: "a place fasih" when it is wide in the gathering.

As-Sulami, al-Hasan and ʿAsim read "fi al-majalis" (فِي الْمَجالِسِ) with an alif, in the plural. Qatadah read "tafasahu" (تفاسحوا) with an alif in both places. The rest read "tafassahu" (تَفَسَّحُوا) "in the gathering," meaning the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Hatim and Abu Ubayd preferred this, saying: "Because it is the common reading, and because 'the gathering' conveys the meaning of all gatherings, including the gathering of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and others."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: al-Qati'i told us: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us: my father told us: Abd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr told us: Fulayh told us, from Ayyub ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Saʿsaʿa [al-Ansari, from Yaʿqub] (the manuscript has a blank here, and the full chain is taken from Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal) ibn Abi Yaʿqub, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Let no man rise from his place and then sit in it again; rather, make room, and Allah will make room for you." [236] [Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal 5/483.]

Abu al-ʿAliya and al-Qurazi said: This refers to the gatherings of war and the positions of fighting. A man would come to the people in the battle line and say to them: "Make room," but they would refuse him out of eagerness for fighting. So Allah commanded them to make room for one another. This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Hasan said: It has reached me that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought the polytheists and arranged his Companions for battle, they would jostle for the front row so as to be at the first assault of the enemy. A man among them would come to the front row and say to his brothers: "Make room for me, so that I may meet the enemy and attain martyrdom." But they would not make room for him, out of their eagerness for jihad and martyrdom. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

﴿And when it is said, "Rise up" (unshuzu), then rise up﴾. ʿAsim, the people of Medina and the people of Syria read the two shin with a damma (unshuzu), while the rest read them with a kasra (inshizu). They are two dialects. The meaning: "When it is said to you, 'Stand up, move, rise, and make room for your brothers,' then do so."

Most of the exegetes said: Its meaning is: when it is said to you, "Rise to prayer, to jihad, to remembrance, or to any good deed," then ﴿rise up﴾ and do not fall short.

ʿIkrima and al-Dahhak said: That is, when the call to prayer is made, stand up for it. This is because some men were sluggish about the prayer when it was called, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Zayd said: This is about the house of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because each man among them loved that his last meeting be with the Messenger of Allah. So Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when it is said, "Rise up"﴾ from the Prophet (ﷺ) and that he has needs, ﴿then rise up﴾ and do not seek to remain with him. ﴿Allah will raise those who have believed among you﴾ by their obedience to the Messenger of Allah, their rising from their gatherings, and their making room for their brothers, ﴿and those who have been given knowledge﴾ among them by the virtue of their knowledge and their precedence, ﴿by degrees.﴾ So Allah, glorified is He, informed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was right in what he commanded, that those believers are rewarded for what they carried out, and that the men from the People of Badr deserve the honor they were given. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn ʿAmir al-Balkhi informed us: al-Qasim ibn ʿAbbad told us: Salih ibn Muhammad al-Tirmidhi told us: al-Musayyab ibn Shurayh told us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Masʿud recited this verse: ﴿Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾, and then said: "O people, understand this verse, and let it encourage you toward knowledge, for Allah, glorified is He, says: Allah raises the believing scholar above the one who does not know, by degrees." [Zad al-Masir 7/324.]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid also informed me: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih informed us: Salih ibn Muqatil informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The excellence of the scholar over the martyr is one degree, the excellence of the martyr over the worshipper is one degree, the excellence of the Prophet (ﷺ) over the scholar is one degree, the excellence of the Qur'an over all other speech is like the excellence of Allah over His creation, and the excellence of the scholar over all people is like my excellence over the least of them." [237] [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan 9/418.]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "Whoever death comes to while he is seeking knowledge, between him and the prophets is one degree." [238] [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan 9/418.]

Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ ﴿On the Day when Allah resurrects them all, and they swear to Him as they swear to you﴾, Qatadah said: The hypocrite will swear to Him on the Day of Resurrection just as he swore to his allies in this world. ﴿And they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, they are the liars.﴾

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ya'qub al-Anbari narrated to us, saying: Abu Hanifa Muhammad ibn Hanifa ibn Mahan al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sulaym al-Hujami narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sulayman al-Dabbas narrated to us, saying: The son of the brother of Rawad narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Uyayna, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection a caller will call out: Where are the adversaries of Allah? Then the Qadariyya (the group who deny divine predestination) will stand, their faces blackened, their eyes blue, their mouths askew, their saliva dripping, and they will say: 'By Allah, we did not worship any besides You, not the sun, nor the moon, nor an idol, nor an image, nor did we take any god besides You.'"

Ibn Abbas said: They spoke the truth, by Allah. Shirk came to them from where they did not know. Then Ibn Abbas recited this verse: ﴿And they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, they are the liars.﴾ They, by Allah, are the Qadariyya; they, by Allah, are the Qadariyya.

﴿Shaytan has gained mastery over them and caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Shaytan. Unquestionably, the party of Shaytan are the losers.﴾ Istahwadha: overpowered and gained control.

﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humbled.﴾ Al-asfalin: the lowest.

﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers."﴾ This was because the believers said: "If Allah opens Mecca and Khaybar and what is around them to us, we hope that Allah will grant us victory over the Byzantines and the Persians." Then Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "Do you think the Byzantines and Persians are like some of the villages you have overcome? By Allah, they have more numbers and greater might than that." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Allah has decreed that I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty.﴾ A parallel is His saying: ﴿And已 Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be helped, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victorious.﴾ [Surat al-Saffat 37:171–173.]

﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah...﴾ — the verse — was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a when he wrote to the people of Mecca. We will mention the story in Surat al-Mumtahana, God willing.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy. He was sitting beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) drank water. Abdullah said: "O Messenger of Allah, leave some of your drink for me." He said: "What will you do with it?" He said: "I will give it to my father, perhaps Allah will purify his heart."

He did so and brought it to his father. The father said: "What is this?" He said: "It is from the drink of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). I brought it to you so that you may drink it, perhaps Allah will purify your heart." His father said: "Why didn't you bring me his urine instead?" So he returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to kill my father." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, be gentle with him and treat him well." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 17/307.]

Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that Abu Quhafa insulted the Prophet (ﷺ), so Abu Bakr struck him a blow that knocked him down. Then this was mentioned to the Prophet (peace be upon him), and he said: "Did you do it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do not do it again." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By Allah, if the sword were near me, I would have killed him." Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers...﴾ [Zad al-Masir 7/328.]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated, from Murra al-Hamdani, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, concerning this verse: ﴿even if they were their fathers﴾ — meaning Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah on the day of Uhud; ﴿or their sons﴾ — meaning Abu Bakr, who called his son to single combat on the day of Badr and said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me charge into the first squadron." The Messenger of Allah said to him: "Let us enjoy you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not know that you are to me like my hearing and my sight?" [Asbab Nuzul al-Ayat 278.]

﴿or their brothers﴾ — meaning Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who killed his brother Ubayd ibn Umayr on the day of Uhud; ﴿or their kinsmen﴾ — meaning Umar, who killed his maternal uncle al-As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira on the day of Badr. And Ali, Hamza, and Ubayda killed Utba and Shayba, the sons of Rabi'a, and al-Walid ibn Utba on the day of Badr.

﴿Those He has written within their hearts [the faith]...﴾ The common reading is with a fatha on the kaf and nun. Al-Mufaddal narrated from Asim with a damma on both, in the passive voice. The first is better because of His saying: ﴿and strengthened them﴾ and ﴿and will admit them﴾.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It means He established faith in their hearts, so they are certain and sincere.

It was said: its meaning is ﴿He wrote within their hearts the faith﴾, like His saying: ﴿upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [20:71].

It was said: He decreed faith for them, and mentioned the hearts because they are its place.

﴿And He strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾: and supported them with victory from Him, said al-Hasan. Al-Suddi said: meaning by faith. Al-Rabi' said: by the Qur'an and its proof, as in His saying: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command﴾ [42:52]. Ibn Jarir said: by light, proof, and guidance. It was also said: by mercy. And it was said: He reinforced them with Jibril (peace be upon him).

﴿And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful.﴾ Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan ibn Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: al-Mardas Abu Bilal narrated to us, saying:

Ismail narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Sa'id al-Jurjani, from some of his teachers, who said: Dawud (peace be upon him) said: "My God, who are Your party, and who surrounds Your Throne?"

Allah, glorified is He, revealed to him: "O Dawud, those who lower their gazes, whose hearts are pure, whose palms are clean. Those are My party and those who surround My Throne." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 17/309.]
